name: libdill
workload: Coroutine context switch and coroutine create/terminate cost, libdill master and an optimized branch vs Go and gccgo.
claimed_speedup: Context switch 16 ns (master) / 13 ns (optimized) vs Go 331 ns and gccgo 825 ns on an i7 4770k; create+terminate 44 ns / 25 ns vs Go 237 ns and gccgo 3652 ns.
hardware: Intel i7 4770k; also Core 2 Duo (libdill only)
tradeoffs: C API with structured-concurrency model (bundles, deadlines); not drop-in for Boost.Context or libco; stackful coroutines with its own scheduler and I/O wrappers.
caveats: Baseline is Go, not Boost.Context/Boost.Coroutine/libco; numbers are from a maintainer's performance-analysis issue (first-party), compiler and flags not stated, old 2016-era hardware, no libco or Boost.Context comparison.
found_via: WebSearch: libdill libmill coroutine context switch ns benchmark; then github.com/sustrik/libdill/issues/30

name: libfiber (iqiyi)
workload: Echo-server IOPS (io echo per second) of the libfiber sample vs libmill, Go and libco samples.
claimed_speedup: README Benchmark section states libfiber IOPS compared with libmill, Go and libco, shown only as an image (res/benchmark.png); no numbers on the page.
tradeoffs: Event-loop fiber library (epoll, kqueue, io_uring, IOCP) with hooked system calls and DNS/semaphore helpers; LGPL license; I/O-oriented rather than pure context-switch speed.
caveats: Benchmark is an image only, so direction of the result and magnitude could not be read from the page; no hardware, compiler or flags; first-party; the pure context-switch cost vs Boost.Context is not measured.
found_via: GitHub topic page github.com/topics/coroutine?l=c; then the repo README Benchmark section
